Subject: Finexa - security evidence & buying process next steps

Hi Asha / Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we heard / decision criteria:
- Primary use case: customer-facing assistant for financial planning (latency & accuracy are critical).
- Economics: pilot <= $10k/month, expansion contingent on performance and SOC/compliance sign-off.
- Risk blockers: SOC 2 Type 2, recent pen test, audit log access / retention policy, and data residency.

Stakeholder map (as discussed):
- Economic buyer: Asha Patel (VP Product) — final approval on budget/contract
- Security reviewer: Tom Graves (Head of Security) — technical sign-off on evidence
- Procurement: procurement@finexa.com (for SOW/DPA/PO) 

Immediate asks (can you confirm owners & timing?):
1) SOC 2 Type 2 report (latest) — needed for legal/infosec review
2) Pen test summary or executive findings (recent 12 months preferred)
3) Audit logs export or sample (showing retention and access controls)
4) Answers on data retention policy, encryption at rest/in transit, and KMS usage

Proposed timeline: if we can get the above by EOD Aug 19, Redwood will prepare a draft commercial terms + DPA and schedule security deep-dive with Tom the week of Aug 24.

Next steps from our side: I’ll prepare a concise evidence checklist and a one‑page mutual action plan.

Thanks — looking forward to keeping momentum.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Dylan — good summary. Confirming owners and rough timeline below: 

- SOC 2 Type 2: we have the 2025 report ready (can share). Owner: Tom's team for redaction review. Target: by Aug 19.
- Pen test: vendor conducted in May 2026; we can share the executive summary and remediation status. Owner: Tom. Target: by Aug 19.
- Audit logs: we can export a 30-day sample and a retention policy doc. Owner: Platform Ops. Target: Aug 19.
- Data residency/KMS: we use AWS KMS and store customer data in us-east-1; retention policy is 7 years by default but configurable.

Procurement (procurement@finexa.com) — once the security team sign-offs the evidence, we’ll need Redwood's standard DPA and a simple SOW. Procurement lead is Priya Natarajan (copied on separate thread).

One ask from our side: can Redwood provide a short diagram (1 page) of where data hits your stack and which components we need to attest to? That will speed our internal reviewers.
